"],["a1d1ca114d395ee258860086eda8e8dce1444d56435ab4c1cf3056870b11f670",36,22,"docs/adr/0003-context-first-project-reads.md","ev-d4cfc8ea37c734004a2708fb","project","ADR 0003: Context-first project reads > Invariants","docatlas://source/v2/72905d9d10ad996c66d6f8b9","## Invariants - Finite literal catalog membership, scope, current hashes, and source identity govern reads. - Readiness and `hard_stop=false` are not permission; `hard_stop=true` blocks edits. - `docs_context` denies answer support, availability, and edit readiness. - Useful partial evidence remains usable with honest missing information. - Metadata-only matches cannot qualify visible evidence; final text is rechecked. - Admitted text, hashes, and coordinates survive delivery together. - Complete DTO bytes/tokens and MCP tool-catalog bytes are minimized without fixed 800/6144 ceilings. - Input, bounded source-read/candidate work, lifecycle, and host-session controls remain separate. - Sync without `mutation` performs no writes. Confirmed upserts bind exact source and catalog hashes, a host-selected private store, and the expected generation. - Deleted, stale, and no-longer-admitted members cannot supply current evidence; confirmed sync does not promise physical deletion of unselected stored rows. "],["c26175b260a6693ca719d1c3059d786793a560725b7bf5998f8940a5174a930c",100,37,"docs/adr/0003-context-first-project-reads.md","ev-d8302fd4125ea5ae338b568f","project","ADR 0003: Context-first project reads > Literal partial body context","docatlas://source/v2/4c127db196daf259c1234f84","## Literal partial body context Partial context is an additional admission for original project reads through `get_docs_context`, not whole-question qualification. Canonical source, scope, version, explicit identity and body-window checks remain mandatory. Missing hard-exact terms cannot be excused by a low whole-question lexical ratio. `ordinary_body_clause_context_v1` uses a contiguous span of the unchanged question with at least two distinct literal words. All words in that span must appear in order inside one substantive source clause; source insertions are allowed. It does not delete function words, short words or query modifiers. `literal_body_block_context_v2` additionally permits a complete technical term and a separate literal query term in one substantive structural body block. Parts of one composed identifier cannot count as two independent terms. Neither witness proves an unmatched modifier or the whole question's relation. Paragraphs, individual list items, code bodies and individual table data rows can supply body context. Headings, links, table headers and fence markers cannot supply these body witnesses. Source bytes and coordinates survive formatting. Unresolved names must occur in the verified current structural owner's scope, or the current body when no owner exists. A bare name may match the first underscore namespace segment for context only; this does not establish exact symbol identity or a subject relation. Query numbers, including numbers next to sentence punctuation, must occur in the same witnessing body block. There is no word dictionary, minimum word length, stemming, synonym expansion, generated lookup or new provider/dependency. The existing conservative clause boundary grammar only rejects phrase joins. Stored queries and canonical hard-exact extraction do not change. Common literal phrases can still be weak relevance signals; this lane is not semantic answer validation. Every partial-body witness requires a private receipt from this exact original query's actual native body discovery. The receipt binds the host-requested local project identity independently of the candidate, the finite current catalog member, generation, source/file hashes and complete returned window span/hash. Fresh source preparation by the owning native context is required; serialized metadata and lookup-only discovery cannot mint that receipt. The receipt exists only for the synchronous public handler, including final projection. Nested calls receive fresh state; normal and exceptional exits deactivate it, including copied contexts. This process-local ledger guards normal consumer replay; it is not a capability against arbitrary Python code. Admission retains the whole acquired source window and its provenance. Projection prefers a complete verified containing section around each admitted seed, then minimizes the packet among equally complete alternatives. Every expansion must retain the original occurrence and rebind its exact source bytes, hash and coordinates. Already visible canonical spans are excluded before spending optional work on additional document-local blocks. For an existing nonempty read-context packet, a selected inspection range can be delivered immediately when its entire text is still unread and already present in the verified snapshot. The same source checks, exact occurrence retention and final validation apply; no additional source read is performed. Otherwise the selected `read_next` remains available. This does not promote empty results or consume a requested-part recovery obligation. Qualification remains false, original-query coverage remains missing, and answer/edit authority remains false. A question mentioning an unknown ordinary modifier may still receive partial context when a real literal phrase matches. Existing explicit-literal and unrelated-empty controls remain required. The main-flow integration check preserves the ten frozen questions and source bytes, independently checks required facts and source/hash/span binding, and keeps public negative reads for a foreign section owner and an absent numeric condition. This evidence does not establish installed-client or production behavior. "],["b932a934838d0b60de576bc8ae58b7a344aa126f5e0ad04846e14b69af5ef896",16,1,"docs/index-cleanup.md","ev-526d7e7628bb359ee941ab61","project","Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely","docatlas://source/v2/5fd1933fb5b5b5bc1526af95","# Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely `doc-atlas clear-index` removes derived index state while preserving project sources, `docatlas.yaml`, configuration, and unrelated files; it never silently widens the cleanup scope. The command is preview-only unless `--apply` is supplied. `clear-index` supports exactly two scopes: `project-local` and `global`. Quarantine is the same-filesystem staging area used before final deletion so moved targets can be restored if the move phase fails. In `clear-index`, `--allow-incomplete` acknowledges that reported unverified vector or cache state will remain; it never bypasses live-process blockers or authorizes remote deletion. `clear-index` deletes only derived SQLite, extracted-document, cache, and verified local vector state. `clear-index` preserves project sources, `docatlas.yaml`, configuration, and unrelated files. "],["58a560ad2d445ed7f019d3297bce169780a29987967a433a8885ed193ce4d973",63,17,"docs/index-cleanup.md","ev-ea55006d75fcd520a91a8a63","project","Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely > Clear one project-local index","docatlas://source/v2/9c2d159fef5ce9b7c36b8164","## Clear one project-local index A project-local cleanup requires a project whose `docatlas.yaml` resolves to that project's `.docatlas` directory: ```bash doc-atlas clear-index \ --scope project-local \ --project-path /absolute/path/to/project \ --format json ``` The preview reports a deterministic `plan_digest`, every recognized target, and any incomplete or blocking condition. Review the preview, stop the Docs MCP server and synchronization workers that use the same storage, then apply the same plan: ```bash doc-atlas clear-index \ --scope project-local \ --project-path /absolute/path/to/project \ --plan-digest \ --apply \ --format json ``` The project-local plan may include: - the configured SQLite database and its `-wal`, `-shm`, and `-journal` sidecars; - the configured extracted-document directory; - project-owned docs, library, embedding, and sqlite-vec cache directories below the resolved project storage root; - a local managed-Qdrant directory only when its ownership marker identifies it as DocAtlas-managed state. Project sources and `docatlas.yaml` are not cleanup targets. A later `prepare_docs(action="sync_project_docs")` can rebuild the index from the reviewable repository files. `project-local` is intentionally limited to a dedicated project-local `.docatlas` root. It refuses projects that resolve to the shared/global index; DocAtlas does not delete one project's rows from a shared database by guessing ownership. Use `--scope global` to reset that shared local index, or give each project an explicit project-local `docatlas.yaml` when independent cleanup is required. "],["823cba175fedb7a03106b7c93219588ead25d619b35cb970663097427a3ace53",86,64,"docs/index-cleanup.md","ev-747f1b761a6e04f4c9df4737","project","Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely > Clear all local indexes while preserving configuration","docatlas://source/v2/5c6c32c3a91dc8454c01479e","## Clear all local indexes while preserving configuration Use the global index scope when the goal is to remove derived indexes under the resolved DocAtlas home while preserving configuration and unrelated files: ```bash doc-atlas clear-index --scope global --format json ``` Apply the reviewed plan with its digest: ```bash doc-atlas clear-index \ --scope global \ --plan-digest \ --apply \ --format json ``` This is intentionally different from `doc-atlas clear`, which remains the broader destructive reset command and may remove configuration and model caches. "],["1ff69fcac713aeab5261175ad418c59e10aba9ea603b4440f889483730f0f3b4",101,87,"docs/index-cleanup.md","ev-8909d31657c90d682369e256","project","Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely > Safety rules","docatlas://source/v2/d594d7dfb64d8d31a752a37b","## Safety rules - Preview does not create a missing storage home or an empty database. - If the preview plan is stale, execution refuses to apply it before any destructive move; a stale `plan_digest` or changed target fingerprint cannot be applied. - `clear-index` refuses to apply a cleanup plan while a live DocAtlas, MCP, synchronization, or managed-Qdrant process holds the index; a recorded live PID is a hard blocker. `--allow-incomplete` does not bypass this live-process blocker. - Targets are moved into same-filesystem quarantine before final deletion. If the move phase fails, already moved targets are restored. - Filesystem roots, the user's home directory, and the current working directory cannot be selected as the DocAtlas storage root. - `clear-index` never deletes remote Qdrant collections. Local vector state without an ownership marker is reported as incomplete and retained. - `--allow-incomplete` only acknowledges that reported vector or cache state will remain; it never bypasses live-process blockers or authorizes unverified or remote deletion. "],["b7a4d1742962789a52c4d3826c5ff4d0322086b082040d4cc05a8560d349c458",121,102,"docs/index-cleanup.md","ev-cf8afaca2c4861ab25e91429","project","Cleaning DocAtlas index state safely > Safety rules > Coordination with index writers","docatlas://source/v2/45fef8fc2465fb57b867893d","### Coordination with index writers Storage mutation coordination is fail-closed: a project sync or library refresh registers a writer lease, while `clear-index` takes the cleanup barrier and refuses cleanup while any live writer lease exists. The short per-database mutation lock is used only around publication/removal, so independent fetch/staging work is not serialized for its full duration. `remove_library_docs` refuses removal while a library-refresh writer lease is active; after the barrier is clear it takes the per-index mutation lock before deleting SQLite/extracted state. Writer leases from dead processes are cleaned during the barrier check; an unreadable lease remains a blocker rather than being ignored. For an MCP client, the same operation remains available through the existing three-tool surface: ```text prepare_docs( action="clear_index", scope="project-local", project_path="/absolute/path/to/project", ) ``` The first response requires confirmation and returns the bound `plan_digest`. The confirmed call must send that digest back so a changed preview cannot be applied accidentally. "],["e4f76e035e165b6b05960c338a3734792236a83ec8b6c812e90c3060587c4f9e",6,1,"docs/main-flow-evaluation.md","ev-97f6b6e6fdc7cf4b65a0569c","project","Оценка основного потока: результат, источники и трасса","docatlas://source/v2/6db68ebbfd7da3f4755bbc4c","# Оценка основного потока: результат, источники и трасса Исследовательская записка, 11 октября 2026 года. Ниже — предложение проверки, а не отчёт о реализованных сценариях или полученном PASS. **Главный вывод:** прохождение проверки-прокси не доказывает решение исходной задачи. Для DocAtlas критерием служат независимо заданные факты документов, допустимые источники и фактическое состояние. Логи помогают объяснить результат, но не являются оракулом корректности. "],["fc9ffed09e491ab7baea2b7a7e0d2e8136f88d44629dfa190bf4193bc5fda1d5",16,7,"docs/main-flow-evaluation.md","ev-3c90f68dacb0a5ac4a74f257","project","Оценка основного потока: результат, источники и трасса > Что подтверждают источники","docatlas://source/v2/928e60715241ea4cacce9e61","## Что подтверждают источники - **[Countdown-Code, arXiv:2603.07084v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.07084v3), §§2–4.** В эксперименте модель может менять как условие в `solution.py`, так и верификатор `test.py`. Поэтому `Rproxy=1` (проверка прошла) совместимо с `Rtrue=0` (исходная арифметическая задача не решена). Истинная оценка использует исходное условие и скрыта от модели при обучении. Около 1% загрязнённых SFT-примеров — фактически 1,2% в отфильтрованном наборе — оказалось достаточно, чтобы у ряда исследованных моделей последующее RL резко усилило reward hacking. Это результат конкретной среды, моделей и обучения, а не универсальный порог. - **Граница Countdown-Code.** Это исследование обхода награды при доступном для записи верификаторе, а не сравнение unit- и integration-тестов. Перенос на HumanEval/LeetCode (§5) оценивали отдельным монитором; прохождение видимых тестов при провале скрытых само по себе не объявляется reward hacking. Работа не доказывает, что интеграционный тест автоматически надёжен или что любой ошибочный ответ является намеренным обходом. - **[Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents), 09.01.2026.** Разделены transcript и outcome: сообщение об успешном действии не заменяет проверку конечного состояния. Рекомендованы реальные задачи, изоляция попыток, устойчивые к обходу graders, проверка фактов, полноты и качества источников, чтение трасс для разбора сбоев. Статья прямо допускает unit-тесты для coding agents; запрета на них из неё не следует. - **[Anthropic: How we built our multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system), 13.06.2025.** Оценка исследовательского результата включает фактическую точность, корректность цитат, полноту и качество источников; приложение рекомендует проверять конечное состояние. Production tracing помогал различать плохой запрос, выбор источника и отказ инструмента. Это инженерный опыт конкретной системы, не доказательство качества DocAtlas и не требование фиксировать единственную последовательность вызовов. - **[Anthropic: Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents), 19.12.2024.** Рекомендованы простые решения, обратная связь от реальной среды, ясные интерфейсы инструментов и усложнение только при измеримом улучшении результата. Прозрачность исполнения полезна, но сама по себе не подтверждает выполнение требований. **Решение проекта:** новые проверки только интеграционного уровня и выше, согласно [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). Это локальная стратегия проекта, а не экспериментальный вывод перечисленных публикаций. "],["5c1b16761247c34f5c176474de7af7d2d191d6d67c66ea6795648675a1687888",27,17,"docs/main-flow-evaluation.md","ev-1d1d4d4953794fbbc3282feb","project","Оценка основного потока: результат, источники и трасса > Предлагаемый публичный сценарий logging off/on","docatlas://source/v2/01b4167b5e11b9a65a7f4b3f","## Предлагаемый публичный сценарий logging off/on Сначала расширить подходящий существующий интеграционный сценарий. Воспроизвести один исходный пользовательский вопрос через настоящий публичный API/CLI/MCP, предпочтительно установленного пакета, на изолированных данных и с реальными retrieval, selection, storage и validation. 1. **Независимый эталон.** До запуска зафиксировать исходный вопрос, corpus и его версии, обязательные факты, дословные опорные фрагменты, допустимые источники/hash/span, scope и ожидаемые изменения состояния. Получить эталон из исходных документов и требований, не из выдачи проверяемого кода. Проверяемый поток не должен переписывать эталон или критерии ради PASS. 2. **Две сопоставимые попытки.** Запустить поток с подробными логами off и on из двух одинаковых исходных состояний, включая индекс, cache, права и consent. Не использовать результат первого запуска как ожидаемый ответ второго. 3. **Два независимых PASS и паритет.** В обоих режимах проверить обязательные факты, исходный текст и соответствие цитат документам; затем сравнить выбранные источники, scope/version, продуктовый результат и изменения состояния. Одинаковые неправильные ответы не дают PASS. Переключатель логов не должен менять права, выбор источников, побочные действия или число продуктовых вызовов. Технические timestamps/trace IDs исключать из сравнения только по заранее заданному правилу. 4. **Диагностический контракт.** При on трасса должна позволять связать этапы одного вопроса и локализовать причину сбоя; пропуски трассы должны быть явными. При off подробная трасса отключена. В MCP диагностический канал отделён от protocol stdout. Наличие события, внутреннего флага или exit 0 не заменяет проверку результата и состояния. Внутренние mocks не использовать. Если для воспроизводимости подменяется внешний транспорт, явно указать эту границу: такой запуск не доказывает работоспособность живого провайдера. "],["07d7f3747a2aab2cb47d146c160c122754b9ec5099a401e4c2a5e5ff4c0035c5",38,28,"docs/main-flow-evaluation.md","ev-64670403bb0b331bdf236f5c","project","Оценка основного потока: результат, источники и трасса > Репрезентативные отрицательные проверки","docatlas://source/v2/4708d1bdb1a27eb254892eae","## Репрезентативные отрицательные проверки Использовать небольшое число публичных сценариев с контролируемыми данными, без матриц строковых вариантов: - **Неверная версия/scope:** добавить похожий документ с конфликтующим фактом вне разрешённой области; ответ обязан опираться на допустимый оригинал. - **Нет достаточного основания:** убрать подтверждающий документ; ожидается предусмотренное контрактом сообщение о нехватке данных, без выдуманного факта или цитаты. - **Нет доступа/consent:** обратиться к недоступному источнику; проверить отсутствие утечки и неразрешённых изменений состояния в обоих режимах. - **Ошибка зависимости или записи логов:** создать отказ на внешней границе; проверить контракт ошибки/восстановления и фактическое состояние. Отказ диагностики не должен менять продуктовый исход относительно такого же запуска без подробных логов. Для каждого случая заранее задать ожидаемый исход и существенный дефект, который проверка должна обнаружить. Сбой разбирать по трассе исходного вопроса, сохраняя неизменными вопрос и критерии. В отчёте фиксировать сценарии, реальные вызовы, время, обнаруженные дефекты и непроверенные границы; количество assertions и объём логов не являются мерой качества. "],["b8f54b567841c823a1b499aeb00b6907100aebc8d5c6c88fc0d8ab060c3ba0c6",88,44,"docs/main-flow-logging.md","ev-425ecab691419d3d284145e9","project","Логи основного потока > Где потерян найденный фрагмент","docatlas://source/v2/235bf89c68e7dc384cc65a58","## Где потерян найденный фрагмент В `docatlas_query_trace` поле `projection_observation.returned_core_diagnostics.context_flow` сохраняет последовательность уже выполненных преобразований контекста: - `core.output`, `decoration.output`, `joint.output`, `query_block.output`, `recovery.output` — состав источников после каждого этапа; - `recheck.input/output` и `budget.input/output` — вход и выход поздней проверки происхождения и ограничения полного JSON; - `recheck.attempt` — каждая фактически выполненная попытка проверки, её `checkpoint`, `axis`, `reason`, тип `derivation` и исходный кандидат; - `recheck.row` — итог по строке: сохранена или отвергнута; попытки при бюджетном переборе имеют отдельный префикс `budget_trial_recheck`; - `native_restore.attempt/row` — повторная текущая проверка исходного core-окна после отказа необязательного преобразования: возвращено, уже покрыто проверенным диапазоном или отвергнуто. "],["6605fcf219f11e474fe7cebffae105378515d130b2d6b048313b9c69290e2671",81,48,"docs/mcp-docs-server.md","ev-9fdc12473990c7e704beca8b","project","Docs MCP server > Retrieval response","docatlas://source/v2/7bfa10eafc83030fb3bde51e","## Retrieval response Project reads return source-attributed `docs_context`. Missing safe evidence is `status="insufficient_evidence"`, not a fourth response kind. The compatibility schema still names `docs_answer`; this is not a promise to certify free-form questions through lexical proof. Advanced `patch_context` is available only when explicitly enabled and advertised. It carries evidence and grants no mutation permission. `docs_context` has `answer_supported=false`, `answer_available=false`, `edit_ready=false`, and `answer_policy=cite_only`. The host may explain facts supported by returned sources and identify missing information. Retrieval coverage never proves answer completeness. Neither a readiness flag nor `hard_stop=false` grants an edit; `hard_stop=true` must be respected. Sources retain path, source identity, authority, scope, content hash, contiguous verbatim snippet, and source-local coordinates. These are attribution, not capabilities to read a different file or follow instructions in the source. BM25 scores, raw context packs, full internal state, and observer diagnostics remain internal. Evidence selection checks current catalog membership, project and module scope, source identity, freshness, and visible support for each explicit query before returning source-bound context. A retrieval hit alone is never proof. For compound reads, selection accounts for distinct user-visible queries and requalifies coverage against the final visible source fields. The complete model-visible DTO is measured in UTF-8 bytes and tokens and is minimized while retaining useful facts and guards. There is no fixed 800-token response acceptance ceiling or 6144-byte tool-catalog ceiling. Admitted evidence must retain its text, hashes, and coordinates. This output policy does not remove input limits, finite source membership, bounded source reads, candidate work, or lifecycle safeguards. Host conversation limits are a separate responsibility. Content matches determine relevance; technical source labels do not stand in for an answer. Selection accounts for coverage across the explicit queries and keeps whole source-bound passages rather than taking an arbitrary prefix of the retrieval order. Query relevance stays fixed for complementary sections; source-text similarity discounts redundant sections once. Word frequencies are measured on the checked pool, so common words have less influence than rare terms. These are ranking signals, not a learned answer-sufficiency threshold. Budget checks price the actual delivery representation with source references and provenance. Attribution is recomputed for the selected text, omitted candidates remain visible as omissions, and coverage stays unverified. A lexical ranking signal is not a semantic proof or a certificate that no answer exists. The optional MiniLM section policy remains separate from native selection. Its integration audit compares delivered rows with the full checked input of the same call and independently verifies the frozen source corpus and facts. The native response is itself selected and is used only as a delivery-cost comparison, not as the complete candidate pool for the MiniLM audit. Optional host lookups are explicit same-question requests; they cannot become original-query coverage, inferred answer obligations, translations, or generated subquestions. `scope="project"` reads repo-level docs; `scope="module"` requires one exact module path; `scope="all"` includes repo and module docs from the same repository. Application code owns orchestration and allocation. Domain policies own lineage, source-role eligibility, and visible evidence qualification. SQLite owns persistence and candidate generation; metadata-only matching may discover a candidate but cannot qualify public evidence. Neither infrastructure nor the MCP adapter decides answer support. Lexical retrieval treats the original document text and headings as content. Catalog descriptions are separate routing information; scope labels, source class labels, and absolute storage paths are not content matches. Existing indexes remain readable without an implicit rebuild or preparation operation. Identifiers keep their literal word boundaries: `action` does not match `next_action`, and a metadata occurrence of `source_of_truth` cannot turn an unrelated `of` in the body into a content match. The original quoted FTS query grouping is retained; the stricter source-field check runs before acquisition limits are applied. The original question and explicit translations/lookups share a final selection step after their candidates have been combined and source-checked. An explicit document filename or relative source path remains a separate routing signal. It is resolved against the complete allowed generation before the candidate limit; an ambiguous basename is not resolved from a shortened hit list. Final selection rechecks the source-reference binding against the current snapshot. Naming a document does not establish a match in its body or increase original-query coverage. "],["45ce1eea0f6c553aeb10dc6bcb7eaf4d837ca2e19f398cfa53f7eaacf5619f87",87,70,"docs/modules/project-context-retrieval.md","ev-abcb64197b2e14a32060c195","module","Project context retrieval module > MCP adapter and fidelity","docatlas://source/v2/1872cce114fa49e920da87d2","## MCP adapter and fidelity The adapter exposes source-attributed `docs_context` for project reads. It measures the complete representation, including public source references, rather than estimating source text alone. Selected passages are not clipped to make them fit. Omitted candidates and unverified coverage remain explicit; a delivered packet is not a completeness claim. Input, source-read, candidate-work, and lifecycle safety bounds remain distinct controls. An explicitly provisioned MiniLM section selector retains its own selection policy. Source continuation cursors are issued only for the selected batch, within the reader's existing capacity. Retaining a previously issued selected cursor does not refresh its expiry or read budget. The final packet is priced again after binding; the source reader still checks current scope, membership and hashes. "],["e52e4e5ba9e191d853eb919158bff35ce15bb638d547f933cd2659f5109e4f58",2,1,"docs/opencode-compact-text.md","ev-1ca39fe04b7bbad871720f93","project","OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text","docatlas://source/v2/24283a634e84ca36db429368","# OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text "],["401beba91bd7dd8e8e5813eafe028de959b3a610aba30e0300a5df04199782ea",35,3,"docs/opencode-compact-text.md","ev-b4af38aadfa329bc288aed51","project","OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text > Installation and normal use","docatlas://source/v2/092f01b63dc9441145bf4679","## Installation and normal use The default `doc-atlas install opencode` registration now sets both `DOCATLAS_MCP_TEXT_FALLBACK=1` and `DOCATLAS_MCP_COMPACT_TEXT=1`. Updating the package alone **does not edit existing OpenCode configuration**; restart OpenCode after registration. This changes only OpenCode's registered DocAtlas MCP environment, not other MCP consumers or selection policies. When the compact-text flag is active, **Context Assembly defaults to `adaptive`** after upgrading to a package containing this change and restarting the MCP server. It may put columns and source-group indexes in the model-visible JSON, with a self-contained reading legend and the original source refs, paths and line ranges. The agent passes the unchanged question and the selected workspace's known absolute `project_path`, or an explicit registered `library`. It does not need to load a skill, enumerate tools again or call `docs_status` before each read. The optional documentation-language mode still requires its scoped language metadata when unknown. Installed guidance adds the short workflow; repair, preparation and advanced patch details remain in guides loaded only when needed. Global installation writes the optional OpenCode skill. `--project` writes a managed repository instruction block and its guides, preserving other text. These are separate instruction surfaces: do not add their measurements to the tool catalog as if every client always injects all of them. "],["b7c072199f7cf199fc95a2edc4ff00bae19ce89c0e017ff622dfeb4f95c2ca04",71,36,"docs/opencode-compact-text.md","ev-8ed9b9e1a3fd964b5c046518","project","OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text > Why not just set `DOCATLAS_MCP_MODEL_VIEW=1`?","docatlas://source/v2/6d1a38dabf22743fafe2b124","## Why not just set `DOCATLAS_MCP_MODEL_VIEW=1`? That earlier mode transmits a concise `content[].text` plus the complete source packet in MCP `_meta`. The pinned stock OpenCode v2.1.2 adapter in `anomalyco/opencode/packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts` (`toCallToolResult`) retains `structuredContent` and `content`, but drops response `_meta`. `packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts` exposes `content` to the model and parses the text JSON when no output schema is declared. Turning on the private-ledger mode for stock OpenCode would lose the original `source-packet` and make its response-local short references non-resolvable. The new **standalone text** mode has no private dependency: selected source text, its original `evidence_id` (`sources[].ref`), `source_uri`, path, section, line range, project identity, scope, version, authority and trust remain in the text. Denials, errors, edit/lifecycle results and advanced patch packets keep their existing routes. An unsupported ordinary documentation shape can use the complete canonical JSON only if that fallback fits the compact-text budget. `DOCATLAS_MCP_MODEL_VIEW=1` and `DOCATLAS_MCP_COMPACT_TEXT=1` are mutually exclusive. For an immediate rollback, remove/set `DOCATLAS_MCP_COMPACT_TEXT=off` in OpenCode's DocAtlas environment; retain `DOCATLAS_MCP_TEXT_FALLBACK=1`. The compact JSON is a model-facing **view**, not a replacement for a full DocAtlas `docs_context` machine packet or a sufficiency certificate. It does not edit the selected source bytes, widen scope or confer answer/edit authority. Clients requiring the full schema must keep the old JSON text interface. For ordinary successful `docs_context` in this explicitly enabled profile, both compact output and a canonical fallback must fit the existing compact-text budget: `max(o200k_tokens, ceil(UTF-8 bytes / 4)) <= 12000`. The fallback path now uses that check too; previously a failed compact rendering could emit a canonical packet without this check. This does not change source selection, the underlying tokenizer, Context Assembly or private model view. It does not add a limit to advanced v4 patch packets or to consumers with compact text disabled. "],["7bb6b5c9a758fb782b737dd6a1ebb189f246c86d0249350e600f4f1359786354",94,72,"docs/opencode-compact-text.md","ev-fc009da50b9b74df1547e128","project","OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text > Delivery failure is distinct from missing evidence","docatlas://source/v2/99cc6b4e8041a674b3aaaf81","## Delivery failure is distinct from missing evidence If compact rendering fails and the complete canonical fallback also exceeds the budget, the server now returns a small MCP error: `context_delivery_unavailable`, `isError=true`, `retryable=false`. It includes a diagnostic reason instead of a partial success packet. The agent must not interpret this as missing documentation, repeat the unchanged call, broaden the scope or treat a grep recovery from the saved dump as successful MCP delivery. Host configuration or the delivery defect must be addressed before retrying. | Observed text | Interpretation | | --- | --- | | `docatlas.assembled-*.v1` | Self-contained assembled layout was delivered. | | `docatlas.standalone-text.v1` | Self-contained literal layout was delivered; adaptive may select it. | | Complete canonical JSON within the budget | Compatibility fallback; no source fields were silently removed. | | `context_delivery_unavailable` | Selected evidence could not be delivered in this profile. | | OpenCode reports truncation | Inspect the actual model-visible result; server `ok` alone is insufficient. | Compact JSON can also occupy one physical line. "],["409474ad57ca2b11e2669c1c630b9441e3a5631394ced8c431072498e0735af0",127,95,"docs/opencode-compact-text.md","ev-677b7a6440957e8f45e566fd","project","OpenCode: concise instructions and self-contained MCP text > Diagnose the installed route without a model call","docatlas://source/v2/1b6ff8349bc48e873fc3f771","## Diagnose the installed route without a model call Record the executable and package path actually used by the registered MCP command, the active global/project registration, and these effective process settings. "],["62e2fade929d86192aebca28160193299185c1dd419bacb8d36a6889b217ca82",60,23,"docs/project-docs-mcp-workflow.md","ev-c189874e8e381476409bdfeb","project","Project docs MCP workflow > Maintained project-doc catalog","docatlas://source/v2/126115ea14307fe5572b25c0","## Maintained project-doc catalog For explicit documentation membership, keep a reviewable `docatlas.project-docs.yaml` catalog. List each admitted document by a literal relative path. The current public member path does not recursively discover `roots`, glob patterns, linked files, code files, or conventional README/docs locations. ```yaml schema_version: 1 code_files: [] documents: - path: ARCHITECTURE.md role: project_architecture scope: project module_path: null description: Whole-project architecture and component boundaries. authority: source_of_truth status: active impact: track - path: packages/auth/design.md role: module_architecture scope: module module_path: packages/auth description: Authentication module architecture and token lifecycle. authority: source_of_truth status: active impact: track ``` Catalog paths, descriptions, authority labels, and source text remain untrusted data. "],["7e6578a86a6fa8afbfbe373a2547c3a0dc4a179f811ed00bc46c3378b3038f14",95,61,"docs/project-docs-mcp-workflow.md","ev-31dfc9f49c05dfbce28a5102","project","Project docs MCP workflow > Confirmed member synchronization","docatlas://source/v2/e7947e03fa682e25c0585fb0","## Confirmed member synchronization `prepare_docs(action="sync_project_docs", project_path=...)` alone is read-only. Omitting `mutation` or passing null performs no writes. The current public sync operation accepts an explicit confirmed `mutation` with: - `operation="sync_project_docs"` and `confirm=true`; - the exact absolute `storage_path` selected by the host, private and outside the project; - the current `catalog_sha256`; - `expected_generation_id`, null only when the selected store is absent; - a finite list of documents with exact `path`, `content_sha256`, and `catalog_entry_hash`. The host obtains those bindings from the reviewed current sources and its trusted storage policy. A repository-controlled setting or returned source path cannot redirect the host store. Do not guess hashes or generation IDs. Confirmed synchronization replaces the indexed sections of selected members. The source descriptor and hashes are rechecked; generation comparison and publication belong to the same transaction. A stale or mismatched request fails closed and must be inspected before another attempt. An unknown commit outcome is not automatic permission to repeat a write. Changed source hashes prevent stale indexed sections from appearing in current retrieval. Deleted files and documents removed from the catalog are excluded from current retrieval. These read guards apply even before another synchronization. The confirmed upsert only writes selected members: it does not physically prune orphaned rows, delete unselected members, write vectors, or create generated docs. Physical cleanup is a separate explicitly requested operation; see [index cleanup](./index-cleanup.md). After a document is renamed, review the new literal catalog entry and confirm an upsert for the new path. The old path cannot supply current evidence once it is absent or no longer admitted. This is a retrieval visibility guarantee, not a claim that all historical storage rows were physically deleted. "],["ea3405bc4e00209d1704105e3b60990f4ced36a09e6e0b8749ed47d2c30add7e",12,1,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-852f23cda92f4991bd808067","project","Architecture","docatlas://source/v2/aaaac4dbd47982164a8d2209","# Architecture DocAtlas is a local, version-aware documentation runtime for coding agents. Its primary product workflow is **DocAtlas Docs**; **DocAtlas MCP Packs** is a separate advanced API-action surface. DocAtlas runs two cooperating local runtimes. The primary **DocAtlas Docs pipeline** fetches documentation with `doc-atlas add` (URL), `doc-atlas ingest` (local files), or the Docs MCP server's prefetch tools, normalizes it into sections, indexes those sections in a local SQLite FTS5 database plus a managed local Qdrant for dense and sparse vectors, and retrieves compact context packs through the CLI or Docs MCP tools. No hosted query API; the only background process is the docmancer-owned Qdrant. The advanced **DocAtlas MCP Packs runtime** installs version-pinned API packs from a registry with `doc-atlas install-pack @`, then exposes every installed pack to your agent through a single shared stdio MCP gateway (`doc-atlas mcp packs-serve`) using the Tool Search pattern: two meta-tools regardless of how many packs you install. The dispatcher enforces auth, destructive-call gating, schema validation, idempotency-key auto-injection and reuse, version pinning on the wire, and SHA-256 verification of every artifact before install. For the full command reference, see [Commands](./Commands.md). For configuration options, see [Configuration](./Configuration.md). "],["ece5778d579a5f6686a70e4a9e54c4881d996afeb239e19e4a1f84dc4c2fab5e",20,13,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-e25f3a6c9e411ef868c5aa33","project","Architecture > Indexing","docatlas://source/v2/5f7cdc5367a71b65a0a31dd8","## Indexing Markdown indexing first normalizes fetched or local documentation into semantic parent sections based on heading structure. The production `parent-child-v1` chunker then splits each parent section into token-bounded child chunks (target 160 estimated visible tokens, hard maximum 512, zero visible overlap) while preserving the parent identity and source offsets. Retrieval ranks those child chunks and can hydrate parent or adjacent context without changing the exact display text. Each section/chunk identity is stored in SQLite with its title, heading path, source URL, content hash, offsets, and token estimate. A FTS5 virtual table indexes retrieval text for fast full-text search. Extracted markdown and JSON files are written to `.docmancer/extracted/` so the indexed content is always inspectable on disk. Alongside the FTS5 index, each section is embedded with FastEmbed (local dense + SPLADE sparse) and upserted into a managed local Qdrant. The dispatcher reads both stores at query time. For which documentation sites and file types work with `add`, see [Supported Sources](./Supported-Sources.md). "],["adc1c5d209e79fc8770229eb96364124d9c0c4952aad162ebe0f9fb6fcfe80dc",35,25,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-34a8f2938e200b4516b979f9","project","Architecture > Project documentation storage and isolation","docatlas://source/v2/e59d39f57efefee35bed1515","## Project documentation storage and isolation Project documentation storage is organized as a derived, project-scoped index of repository-owned files. Each project identity receives isolated SQLite index state in a host-selected private store outside the repository, so one repository's project docs cannot satisfy another repository's query. The filesystem documents remain authoritative; current document and catalog-entry hashes must match the admitted indexed member. Confirmed member upserts are lexical-only and do not publish extracted artifacts. The index is derived state; separate physical cleanup is described in [Index cleanup](../docs/index-cleanup.md). "],["008f277f6dfd9eed4ad952648000bbbbac228524050d94664509edcb0f307e7a",58,42,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-84c597ddbb07af9ea45523c5","project","Architecture > Hybrid retrieval","docatlas://source/v2/e893a526ab94adfaaa253914","## Hybrid retrieval A fresh configuration queries the FTS5 index in `lexical` mode by default. Ingest may also populate dense FastEmbed and SPLADE sparse vectors in Qdrant; select `dense`, `sparse`, or `hybrid` explicitly or set `retrieval.default_mode`. Non-lexical retrieval fails closed when a required capability is unavailable unless the caller opts into degraded fallback with `--allow-degraded`. Components: - **`docmancer.runtime.qdrant_manager`** owns the local Qdrant lifecycle: binary acquisition from the pinned `v1.14.1` GitHub release, port selection under `filelock`, background spawn with telemetry disabled, ownership sentinel, foreign-process refusal, and a `SqliteVecStore` fallback when the platform has no matching binary. - **`docmancer.embeddings`** is the Python import namespace for the embedding providers (`FastEmbedProvider` for local dense + sparse; cloud providers for OpenAI / Voyage / Cohere). A content-hash-keyed disk cache under `~/.docatlas/embeddings-cache/` avoids re-embedding unchanged chunks. The cloud providers retry on 429/5xx with bounded exponential backoff; when a configured cloud provider has no API key in env, ingest falls back to FTS5-only with a warning rather than aborting. - **`docmancer.embeddings.pipeline.sync_vector_store`** reconciles SQLite sections against existing Qdrant points: it skips unchanged content via the `embedding_upserts` bookkeeping table, prunes points whose chunk ids no longer exist in SQLite (so `ingest --recreate` cannot leave stale dense hits behind), embeds the rest in batches, and bulk-upserts. - **`docmancer.stores`** wraps both backends behind a `VectorStore` interface. `QdrantStore.ensure_collection` refuses to claim a pre-existing collection that lacks the docmancer ownership sentinel, and `delete_collection` will only operate on docmancer-owned collections. - **`docmancer.retrieval.dispatch.RetrievalDispatcher`** fans out across `lexical` (FTS5), `dense` (Qdrant or sqlite-vec), and `sparse` (SPLADE in Qdrant) via a thread pool, fuses the per-source ranks with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (vanilla or weighted), and hydrates the top-K section ids back into `RetrievedChunk` rows. Two extensions sit on this path: - **Hierarchical retrieval** (`retrieval.hierarchical.enabled: true`) runs in two stages: a wide-net pass aggregates scores by `document_title_hash` and picks the top documents; a second pass re-retrieves sections filtered to those documents before fusion. - **Query-aware routing** (`retrieval.routers: [...]`) walks an ordered list of regex matchers; the first match merges its declared filters into the dispatcher filters for that call, for example routing API-reference queries to `source_path_prefix=api`. - **Neighbor expansion** plumbs through hybrid mode the same way as lexical: after the top section ids are picked, prev/next siblings are appended so partial bullets arrive with their surrounding context. `doc-atlas query --mode {lexical,dense,sparse,hybrid} --explain` exposes the mode and shows per-source rank contributions (e.g. `lexical#1, dense#3, sparse#2`) under each result. "],["70e71a0f0c7a7f360fb0611d23efed4861e565d4082718a56139272ad648065f",93,68,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-abd646a8b777b9dd756dbff3","project","Architecture > Docs source registry","docatlas://source/v2/67fb9a9505a3e95ac376db6a","## Docs source registry The `LibraryRegistry` is a SQLite-backed persistent store for known documentation sources. Each entry is identified by three levels of identity: - **`source_id`** — identity without version (e.g. `pub:go_router:api`). Used for grouping all versions of one library. - **`canonical_id`** — version-pinned identity (e.g. `pub:go_router@14.8.1:api`). The primary key for upsert and lookup. - **`library_id`** — current canonical identity (aliased to `canonical_id`). Migrated when the naming scheme changes. The registry stores per-entry metadata: | Field | Purpose | |-------|---------| | `version`, `source_type` | Resolution axes | | `docs_url`, `docs_url_template` | Source locator (template supports version interpolation) | | `docs_url_resolved` | Pre-rendered effective URL | | `docs_snapshot_exact` | Whether the indexed docs are an exact version snapshot (not latest/stable) | | `requested_version`, `resolved_version`, `version_source`, `version_confidence`, `version_inferred` | Version provenance audit trail | | `target_spec_json` | Full fetch target specification (seed URLs, allowed domains, path prefixes, etc.) | | `last_refreshed_at`, `last_error`, `status` | Lifecycle tracking | | `legacy_ids_json` | Previous library IDs for backward-compatible lookup | | `aliases_json` | Alternative names used for matching | **Lookup cascade**: `get()` tries exact `library_id` match first, then `canonical_id`, then `legacy_id`, then `(normalized_name + ecosystem + version + source_type)`, then partial matches by alias or legacy ID. This handles both version-precise lookups and fuzzy name resolution. **Migration**: When the canonical naming scheme changes, `migrate_library_id()` renames the entry and stores the old ID in `legacy_ids_json` so existing references still resolve. "],["4fb3eb757ade9de60f0f6a92e142e8c315b59ccba7da6785809a136bea18db98",105,94,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-1287adea1b7137f611a2aefc","project","Architecture > Version-aware dependency resolution","docatlas://source/v2/21998c77f7791923d23cef66","## Version-aware dependency resolution The `ProjectMetadataReader` inspects project metadata to choose the exact documentation version the project uses: - **`.fvmrc`** — reads Flutter SDK version or channel (stable/beta/main). Determines which `api.flutter.dev` docs to fetch. - **`pubspec.lock`** — extracts pinned package versions from `packages` map. Used as exact version sources for pub.dev Dartdoc and docs.rs bindings. - **`pubspec.yaml`** — reads direct dependencies and specifier kinds (exact, range, path, git). - **`Cargo.toml`** / **`Cargo.lock`** — extracts Rust dependency versions and sources (registry, path, git). Non-registry sources produce warnings about inexact docs binding. - **`package.json`** with **`package-lock.json`**, **`pnpm-lock.yaml`**, or **`yarn.lock`** — extracts direct npm dependencies and exact installed versions. `packageManager` chooses the authoritative lockfile when more than one exists; workspace/path/git sources remain explicitly non-registry. The resolution happens in `LibraryDocsService.get_docs()` when `project_path` is provided and `version` is not explicitly set. For Flutter SDK docs, the version is resolved from `.fvmrc`; for pub packages, from `pubspec.lock`; for Rust packages, from `Cargo.lock`. "],["482f3e2e08f2571ae91df570ba2c8732b02028c16580b65bb55800365ef06e1f",120,106,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-6ac6407c07190e4c78c1b731","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime","docatlas://source/v2/f96bf7a6a54a6d2e697ebc7e","## Docs MCP runtime `doc-atlas mcp docs-serve` exposes the docs runtime to coding agents as MCP tools. It uses the same local ingest, index, update, and query path as the CLI, plus the persistent SQLite registry for known documentation sources. For repository coding and patch tasks, agents call `get_docs_context(project_path=..., question=...)` first. Project reads return bounded `docs_context` from finite explicit current membership. Missing safe evidence is `status="insufficient_evidence"`. Compatibility `docs_answer` does not confer lexical answer certification; `patch_context` is an explicitly enabled advanced representation, not automatic output for a coding question or permission to edit. Follow only the exact returned `recommended_next_action` or an explicit user lifecycle request, retaining confirmation and source bindings. After verified success and readiness, retry the original question unchanged. `docs_status` is reserved for explicit health, freshness, index, and job-status requests. The original and explicit host lookups have separate lineage. Public documentation reads do not infer query aliases or authorize implementation-code discovery. Context selection rechecks the visible source identity and text; output bytes and tokens are minimized without a fixed response-size acceptance ceiling. Input, source-read, candidate-work, and lifecycle controls remain distinct. Advanced code and repository-map workflows, when explicitly enabled, do not turn navigation evidence into authoritative policy. If the user asks broadly about "the MCP server", distinguish the two surfaces explicitly: - **Docs MCP server:** `doc-atlas mcp docs-serve` exposes exactly `get_docs_context`, `prepare_docs`, and `docs_status` for the default documentation workflow. - **MCP Packs runtime:** `doc-atlas mcp packs-serve` exposes installed API action packs through `docmancer_search_tools` and `docmancer_call_tool`. These tool names follow the Python/runtime namespace; the MCP server identity is `docatlas`. Legacy direct library/project tools remain internal compatibility paths. They are not a public routing contract for agents; see [Docs MCP server](../docs/mcp-docs-server.md) for the current tool contract. "],["d9603407f41341712637742af3062141af4211d09722afe6133be0d4b7fc2817",126,121,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-7787a837b9c8e2c544405e60","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > Prefetch and job tools","docatlas://source/v2/acb1fa51def95c2ff11874df","### Prefetch and job tools - **`prepare_docs(action="prefetch_docs_manifest", ...)`** — Validate and prefetch targets declared in a `docatlas.docs.yaml`, subject to the applicable authorization and consent. - **`docs_status(action="job", job_id=...)`** — Return progress for one docs indexing/prefetch job. - **`docs_status(action="jobs", ...)`** — List docs indexing/prefetch jobs, optionally filtered by status. - **`prepare_docs(action="cancel_docs_job", job_id=...)`** — Request cancellation for a docs indexing/prefetch job. "],["a336c014dd363010584ef61873c29ed585b9b22eadbac47eb414cd5df7905d27",134,127,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-ed2f6fb08060c5b73d953cfd","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > docs_url template","docatlas://source/v2/631069abeb828f388ebcafa5","### docs_url template The `docs_url_template` parameter supports version interpolation: `template.format(library=library, version=version)`. "],["d8de2a6a558187f66f9924731f18b8d642f2c439b99fa04eb00b21a840ac98e8",149,135,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-4d195f614254323de19550a5","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > Async prefetch and job tracking","docatlas://source/v2/ad7f8e274da1526c722214d2","### Async prefetch and job tracking The corresponding `prepare_docs` prefetch actions may start background work. When they do, the service: 1. Creates a `DocsJob` entry with a UUID4 job ID and `pending` status 2. Starts a daemon background thread to run the fetch/index pipeline 3. Returns immediately with a `DocsJobStartResult` containing the `job_id` The `DocsJobTracker` maintains an in-memory dictionary of jobs (trimmed to `MAX_DOCS_JOB_HISTORY = 100`). Each job tracks: - **Lifecycle**: `status` (pending/running/succeeded/partial/failed/cancelled), `phase` (validating/resolving/fetching/indexing/done), timestamps - **Progress**: `total_targets`, `completed_targets`, `failed_targets`, `current_target`, `current_url` - **Page tracking**: `discovered_pages`, `fetched_pages`, `indexed_pages`, `total_pages`, `completed_pages`, `failed_pages`, `total_chunks`, `completed_chunks` - **Events**: ordered event log with phase, URL, and message per target/page Call `docs_status(action="job", job_id=...)` to poll progress. Jobs can be cancelled via `prepare_docs(action="cancel_docs_job", job_id=...)`; the cancellation flag is checked between targets and between seed URLs during a target. "],["09ffcbbaa65829e0769c43e50586b037392b18108772af403548402b4eb86cfa",181,150,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-1c1834d59eebff334bd0c438","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > docatlas.docs.yaml manifest","docatlas://source/v2/23e5f834f5e27dd22bf03dfa","### docatlas.docs.yaml manifest The manifest is a YAML file that declares a batch of documentation targets: ```yaml version: 2 defaults: source: authority: official_project version_binding: rolling format: html scope: allowed_domains: [docs.example.com] coverage: bounded targets: - id: my-lib identity: {kind: package, ecosystem: python, name: my-lib} version: {requested: "2.1.0", policy: exact} source: type: api url: https://docs.example.com/my-lib/2.1.0/ version_binding: exact scope: {path_prefixes: [/my-lib/2.1.0/]} - id: project-dep identity: {kind: package, ecosystem: pub, name: some-dep} version: {requested: project-version, policy: project, package: some-dep, fallback: latest} source: {type: api, url_template: "https://pub.dev/documentation/{library}/{version}/"} scope: {allowed_domains: [pub.dev], path_prefixes: [/documentation/some-dep/]} ``` `validate_docs_manifest` checks structure, duplicate IDs/`canonical_id`, URL security (no private/localhost URLs, allowed domain validation), source type validity, and `project-version` resolution. `prefetch_docs_manifest` runs validation then delegates to `prefetch_docs_targets`. "],["fdcbae5677f11acd569b2cbb25b8c9347ea0fa3ecfe329f0341a9422fbb01cdb",187,182,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-d600a3c24f909cc2da9eab53","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > Dartdoc discovery","docatlas://source/v2/5f0b19a648bf7e0787422e83","### Dartdoc discovery For pub.dev Dartdoc targets (ecosystem `pub`, source type `api`), the service can automatically discover seed URLs from the package's documentation index page. `discover_pub_dartdoc_seed_urls` parses the package root HTML with BeautifulSoup, extracting entity pages (`-class.html`, `-library.html`, etc.) and library pages. This produces precise seed URLs instead of crawling the entire pub.dev domain, reducing fetch time and network load. Fallback: if discovery fails or returns no URLs, the service falls back to the root documentation URL as a single seed. "],["a4088729ffc6c1108c0ef4267cd5c2efedbd8d677a373961efd8b56648a54119",204,188,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-09f556c826243db9fe5a2904","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > URL security and docs policy","docatlas://source/v2/c7cb2701175ec7df5f63c5d1","### URL security and docs policy All remote URLs pass through security validation: - Only `http`/`https` schemes allowed - Localhost, private network, loopback, link-local, and multicast addresses rejected - URL host must match one of the `allowed_domains` - URL path must match one of the `path_prefixes` (if specified) The docs policy system in `_docs_policy` produces machine-readable WebFetch rules for agents: ```json {"direct_webfetch": "forbidden", "reason_code": "registered_source_exists"} {"direct_webfetch": "discovery_only", "reason_code": "no_registered_source"} ``` Registered sources forbid direct WebFetch (the agent must use DocAtlas). Unknown sources permit discovery-mode WebFetch only. "],["56e694ef2ae46e59aeeedcb8028c70693824bbbc9278fb25e6f1d4d4b92bd48a",218,205,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-1bc0f61333d77076a50d778f","project","Architecture > Docs MCP runtime > Version provenance on every response","docatlas://source/v2/0a4893370b142a0354f2b436","### Version provenance on every response Every `DocsResult` includes a full version identity block: - `requested_version` — what was asked for - `resolved_version` — what was actually resolved - `version_source` — how the version was determined (`explicit`, `project`, `lockfile_exact`, `manifest_exact`, `manifest_range`, `registry`) - `docs_snapshot_exact` — whether the indexed docs are an exact version snapshot - `docs_exactness` — categorized value (`exact_snapshot`, `exact_version_url`, `no_docs`) - `docs_binding_source` — where the docs were bound from (`registry`, `pub_dartdoc`, `docs_rs`, `flutter_api_current_channel`) - `confidence` — high-level confidence indicator - `tool` / `schema_version` — always `get_library_docs` / `2.0-mvp` When the input `docs_url` conflicts with a registered source's stored locator, the service returns `docs_url_conflict` status with the registered source's identity, guiding the agent to retry without `docs_url`. "],["b111b3da0e87eeed096b078eb6ac7640d77cf19de8066f1880c5a81db9e25b2f",222,219,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-3b8a7dc002a66e7b5a8609b2","project","Architecture > Project Docs pipeline","docatlas://source/v2/f45a0118441a1c4a89cbc00a","## Project Docs pipeline The project-aware docs pipeline runs alongside the library docs pipeline, using the same ingestion engine but with project-scoped source classes and metadata. "],["4d883f814972381353855b86fcebc42a9d60c355c1a5459c5027e1b452ad385d",241,223,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-8f364a9938912a3d729d6bee","project","Architecture > Project Docs pipeline > Discovery","docatlas://source/v2/cfdee6df7cdf2081d2d348f4","### Discovery The current public project-docs path requires finite literal entries in `docatlas.project-docs.yaml`. It does not infer read membership from README names, module directories, recursive roots, or Markdown links. Repo-level and exact module membership remain distinct scopes. Reads compare current file and catalog-entry hashes with the indexed member. Changed, deleted, or no-longer-admitted sources cannot supply current evidence. `prepare_docs(action="sync_project_docs")` without `mutation` performs no writes. A confirmed member upsert binds the exact catalog and source hashes, a trusted host-selected store, and the expected generation. It replaces sections only for selected members; physical deletion of unselected rows and vector/artifact writes are outside this public operation. See [Project docs MCP workflow](../docs/project-docs-mcp-workflow.md) for the current preparation and verification sequence. Repository documentation edits remain ordinary reviewable Git changes authorized by the user. "],["feb2f4c2465288e458f39b492e08d8f01bd9871e6deaee9b4d43c0063efba0a7",262,242,"wiki/Architecture.md","ev-32172a6475da839e15e8b1d5","project","Architecture > Packs MCP runtime","docatlas://source/v2/c07e9eab662471e738d0fc89","## Packs MCP runtime `doc-atlas install-pack @` downloads the pack's five artifacts (`contract.json`, `tools.curated.json`, `tools.full.json`, `auth.schema.json`, `provenance.json`) plus a `manifest.json` with SHA-256s, verifies every artifact hash, and writes them under `~/.docatlas/servers/@/`. The package is added to `~/.docatlas/mcp/manifest.json` with per-package state (mode = curated/expanded, allow_destructive, allow_execute, enabled). When an advanced user explicitly launches or registers `doc-atlas mcp packs-serve` for installed API packs, the server exposes exactly **two** tools to the agent regardless of how many packs are installed: - `docmancer_search_tools(query, package?, limit)`: hybrid-ready search across enriched operation metadata (operation ids, summaries/descriptions, aliases, intents, tags, examples, and schema terms). The default remains dependency-light BM25-style lexical ranking with synonym expansion and snake/kebab/camel token normalization. Set `DOCATLAS_MCP_SEARCH=hybrid` plus `DOCATLAS_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL=` to add local semantic embeddings as a second signal; lexical and semantic ranks are fused with RRF, and unavailable semantic search falls back to lexical with an explicit warning. Returns name, description, safety, score/rank metadata, low-confidence search metadata, and inlined `inputSchema` for every returned match. - `docmancer_call_tool(name, args)`: dispatches the resolved tool through the matching executor. Every dispatch passes through the gate chain (in order): 1. **Resolve.** Look up the slug `package__version__operation` (D15: double-underscore field separators, single-underscore intra-field replacement of `.`/`-`/`/`) against the manifest. 2. **Validate.** Run `args` through the operation's `inputSchema` with `jsonschema`. Tool Search hides per-tool schemas from the MCP `tools/list` surface, so the dispatcher must validate (spec 2.8.5). 3. **Auth.** Resolve credentials by precedence: per-call override, process env, agent-config env, then the per-package credential fallback. For OpenAPI `apiKey` schemes, place the resolved value in the right slot per `in: header|query|cookie`. 4. **Safety gate.** If the operation is destructive and the package was not installed with `--allow-destructive`, refuse with a remediation message naming the exact `install-pack ... --allow-destructive` command. If the executor is `python_import` or `shell` and the package was not installed with `--allow-execute`, refuse similarly. 5. **Idempotency.** For non-idempotent operations on sources that declare an idempotency header, generate a UUID4 `Idempotency-Key`. A SQLite fingerprint cache (24 h TTL, key = tool + canonicalized args) reuses the same key on retry; the agent can also pass `args._docatlas_idempotency_key` explicitly. 6. **Execute.** Hand off to the executor (`http`, `noop_doc`, `python_import`). The HTTP executor merges `auth.required_headers` declared in the contract (used by keyed APIs that pin a dated wire version), auth headers/params/cookies, and the per-operation `http.encoding` (`json | form | multipart | query_only | path_only`). Path parameters are percent-encoded as one segment, so values containing `/`, `?`, or `#` do not alter the URL structure. 7. **Log.** Append a redacted entry to `~/.docatlas/mcp/calls.jsonl` (only `arg_keys`, never values). Pack paths are validated and resolved before use: `..` segments, NUL, backslashes, leading `@` in the version, and absolute paths are rejected, and the resolved candidate must remain inside `~/.docatlas/servers`. This keeps a malicious or malformed registry entry from escaping the storage root. The default `doc-atlas ingest` runs the hybrid path: on first ingest it downloads the pinned Qdrant binary, starts it in the background, and embeds + upserts vectors alongside FTS5. Use `ingest --no-vectors` (or set `DOCATLAS_AUTO_VECTORS=0`) for FTS5-only runs. | Subcommand | Description | |------------|-------------| | `doc-atlas qdrant up` | Download the pinned Qdrant binary (currently `v1.14.1`) to `~/.docatlas/qdrant/qdrant` if absent, start it in the background, write a PID + runtime metadata file, and spawn with telemetry disabled (`QDRANT__TELEMETRY_DISABLED=true`). Pass `--port` to pin a specific port, or `--docker` to print a `docker compose` snippet instead of running the managed binary. | | `doc-atlas qdrant down` | Stop a docmancer-managed process. Add `--json` for raw JSON. | | `doc-atlas qdrant upgrade` | Swap the managed binary in-place against the same on-disk storage. Refuses to run against a live docmancer-owned process without `--force`. Cross-version storage migration is not automated. | | `doc-atlas qdrant logs` | Tail the managed binary's stdout (or stderr with `--stderr`) from `~/.docatlas/qdrant/logs/`. | Environment overrides: - `DOCATLAS_QDRANT_URL`: point docmancer at an existing Qdrant (managed elsewhere). Safety: `QdrantStore.ensure_collection` refuses to claim a pre-existing collection that does not carry the docmancer ownership sentinel, and `delete_collection` will only operate on docmancer-owned collections. "],["28218ff98cfa16aa8aedd236619526a68cdbfe9e7622ea9141ff5e513e2502b7",13,12,"wiki/Configuration.md","ev-d430704bf2c604e39a22f9b1","project","Configuration > Configuration Reference","docatlas://source/v2/11a5bcd98852fdd0ada6f427","## Configuration Reference "],["655fce7cd389ee7fb9ea03d543d7feb301f50bf60662100de4edd66e44651ddd",64,49,"wiki/Configuration.md","ev-d99c8a315b56a02006c572a7","project","Configuration > Configuration Reference > Vector store","docatlas://source/v2/1dfe5b95b1549b6646238861","### Vector store A fresh configuration uses `retrieval.default_mode: lexical` for queries. Ingest can auto-start managed Qdrant and embed chunks with FastEmbed; the `vector_store:` block tunes that optional vector store. Select `dense`, `sparse`, or `hybrid` explicitly when vector retrieval is required. Those modes fail closed when required capabilities are unavailable unless the caller explicitly enables degraded fallback. Set `DOCATLAS_AUTO_VECTORS=0` (or run `doc-atlas ingest --no-vectors`) for FTS5-only ingestion. | Key | Default | What it controls | |-----|---------|------------------| | `vector_store.provider` | `qdrant` | `qdrant` (managed local or remote) or `sqlite-vec` (small-scale fallback that needs no separate process) | | `vector_store.url` | unset | Explicit Qdrant URL. The CLI installs the resulting packs with `doc-atlas install-pack @`. | Source standard | What the pipeline does | Executor in the pack | |-----------------|------------------------|----------------------| | **OpenAPI 3.0 / 3.1** | Resolves intra-document `$ref`, infers `http.encoding` from `requestBody.content`, extracts auth schemes (`bearer` / `apiKey` / `oauth2`) and merges per-source overrides. | `http` (live wire calls with auth, headers, idempotency) | | **GraphQL introspection JSON** | Maps queries to read-safe operations and mutations to destructive operations. | `http` (single endpoint, JSON body) | | **TypeDoc JSON** | Emits `noop_doc` operations whose bodies return the documentation snippet for each declared symbol. | `noop_doc` (no live call; documentation only) | | **Sphinx `objects.inv`** | Parses the zlib-compressed inventory format and emits `noop_doc` operations per documented object. | `noop_doc` | | **`python_import` (opt-in)** | Lets a pack run a Python callable in a subprocess against a venv-detected interpreter.
